_comment: Shared fixture for kernel symbol canonicalization. Two implementations must agree on it:
The JS gate and the Python verdict compare the SAME two symbols, so any drift between them lets
a kernel pass one side and be refused by the other. Asserted from Python by
Symbols marked 'real' were lifted verbatim from ROCm captures. Hand-written C++ never produced
the shapes that broke this: an unnamed namespace putting a '(' in front of the kernel, a bare
kernel with no namespace to separate it from the 'void' return type, and the annotations this
pipeline appends to a name after the fact -- a phase tag, a cluster label, a memcpy direction.

canonical.symbol: void aiter::greedy_sample_kernel<float, 1024, 16>(float const*, int*, int, int)

canonical._note: profile artifacts store long kernel names elided mid-template, leaving an opener that never closes
the annotations below are appended by this pipeline, not by the compiler. Reading the name from the END of the symbol answers with the annotation and the head stops matching its own kernel.
rocprof spells memory ops with the direction after the operation
an unnamed namespace can also sit mid-qualification, leaving 'at::native:: ::CatArray...' once the group is removed

matches.why: the bare name and its decorated spelling are one kernel
a bare declared name has no template arguments to compare, so it matches the decorated spelling
two instantiations of one template are two kernels once both sides carry the arguments
real head row: a short_name cut inside the ARGUMENT list keeps a whole template, and only one side spells the return type and namespace
matches.b: void (anonymous namespace)::clamp_position_kernel<long>(long*, long const*, unsigned long, int)

matches.why: one build leaves the namespace unnamed and another declares it; same kernel, same instantiation
both argument lists are elided, so they must agree as far as they are spelled: 128, 4 against 128, 8
folding separators to _ stops '128, 4,' from reading as a prefix of '128, 48,'
real sglang neighbours: a name appearing inside another is a different kernel
a name embedded in another is not evidence of the same kernel
two unnamed-namespace kernels used to both reduce to 'void' and certify each other
a token this short appears inside unrelated kernels and is not evidence
a prefix that is not the display-limit truncation is a different kernel
a name cut at the 60-char display limit ends mid-token, so only a prefix rule can match it
one character short of the display limit is just an unrelated fragment
real head row: the phase tag is ours, so the row still has to match the kernel it names
real head row: a memcpy row and its own rocprof spelling
an empty side is never evidence
